newsitem.title: UK: Camilla's ex says she can wed Charles - UK paper.
newsitem.headline: Camilla's ex says she can wed Charles - UK paper.

text.p: The former husband of Camilla Parker Bowles has told friends he hopes his ex-wife will win public acceptance and marry Prince Charles, heir to the British throne, the Sunday Express newspaper reported.
"Andrew Parker Bowles has confided that he believes public opinion should support the prince in his dream of one day making Camilla his wife," said the paper.
The paper said retired army officer Parker Bowles -- at one time the nation's best-known cuckold -- recently surprised friends at a dinner party by saying: "They would certainly have my blessing."
One diner was quoted as telling the Express on Sunday:

"To many people, it would seem a remarkable and hard-to-believe act of forgiveness after all those painful headlines (detailing the long-running affair between Camilla and Charles). But Andrew has found great happiness in his remarriage and genuinely wants Camilla to discover the same.

"In a sense, he would like to think that if he, of all people, can come to sympathise with Charles' and Camilla's commitment to each other, then one day the future king's subjects will be able to do the same."
Charles admitted committing adultery with Camilla after his separation from Princess Diana in 1992.
Both Charles and Camilla are now divorced and, in theory at least, free to go public with their long-standing love affair.
They are often spotted together at private functions and he is reported to have bought her lavish presents.
But opinion polls continue to reflect the British public's distaste for the earthy woman who captured Charles' heart when he was just 21 and outright hostility to the idea of her ever becoming queen.

The paper said Charles had promised his mother, Queen Elizabeth, that he would not re-marry if it threatened the monarchy. The Express said the couple believed their best chance of wedding would be new love for Diana, mother of Charles' sons.
After the collapse of her marriage to Charles, Diana publicly complained: "There were three of us in this marriage, so it was a bit crowded."
